The Critical Role of Multi-Stage Filtration in Mitigating High-Salinity Borehole Water

Share this article:
WhatsApp LinkedIn Facebook X Email
Link copied to clipboard!

Recirculating Aquaculture Systems (RAS) represent the definitive technological frontier in modern intensive land-based aquaculture. Conventional flow-through systems require millions of litres of pristine river or coastal seawater daily, continuously exposing sensitive stocks to wild seasonal temperature spikes, agricultural pesticide runoff, parasitic vectors, and harmful algal blooms. In stark contrast, an engineered RAS continuously purifies, thermally conditions, aerates, and recycles 90% to 99% of total system water volume through a closed or semi-closed hydrodynamic circuit.

The Engineering Fundamentals: Why Closed Water Recirculation Works

At high commercial stocking densities (ranging from 30 kg/m³ for finicky marine species to upwards of 80–120 kg/m³ for intensive salmonids, catfish, or tilapia), cultured fish and crustaceans excrete substantial quantities of biological wastes: intact solid feces, dissolved total ammonia nitrogen (TAN), carbon dioxide (CO₂), and microscopic organic colloids. Without continuous multi-barrier extraction, these metabolic byproducts rapidly poison the aquatic environment, strip dissolved oxygen, suppress immune response, and induce mass mortality within hours.

A high-performance RAS functions as an artificial, engineered ecosystem. By integrating precision mechanical separation, autotrophic bacterial nitrification, gas stripping, ultra-pure oxygen enrichment, and biological disinfection, operators gain total sovereign control over culture water chemistry regardless of outside environmental turbulence.

The Multi-Barrier RAS Water Treatment Loop

Deep Blue Aqua designs and fabricates turnkey RAS treatment loops tailored specifically to Southern African conditions, where water scarcity, biosecurity, and electrical grid volatility are top priorities. Every facility incorporates a synchronized succession of primary, secondary, and tertiary unit operations:

1. Primary Mechanical Separation (Rotary Drum Filters)

Solid removal is the single most critical step in RAS management. Solid feces and uneaten pelleted feed must be physically extracted from the water column within minutes before hydraulic turbulence and biological decay dissolve them into colloidal particles and toxic ammonia. Stainless steel (316L) micro-screen drum filters with mesh apertures between 40 µm and 60 µm filter the entire tank volume once every 30 to 45 minutes, reducing biological oxygen demand (BOD) loads on the downstream biofilter by up to 50%.

2. Biological Nitrification (Moving Bed Biofilm Reactors - MBBR)

Dissolved unionized ammonia (NH₃) is intensely toxic to aquatic organisms even at concentrations as low as 0.05 mg/L. In the MBBR, billions of aerobic nitrifying bacteria colonize specialized high-surface-area virgin polypropylene carrier media (providing 650 to 900 m²/m³ of protected surface area). The two-step biological oxidation proceeds under continuous coarse aeration:

  • Step 1 (Nitrosomonas spp.): Converts total ammonia nitrogen into toxic nitrite: NH₄⁺ + 1.5 O₂ → NO₂⁻ + H₂O + 2H⁺
  • Step 2 (Nitrobacter / Nitrospira spp.): Rapidly oxidizes nitrite into relatively harmless nitrate: NO₂⁻ + 0.5 O₂ → NO₃⁻

Because nitrification produces hydrogen ions (H⁺) that consume system alkalinity, automated sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO₃) or calcium carbonate dosing ensures pH remains stable between 7.2 and 7.6, preserving bacterial conversion rates.

3. Micro-Colloid & Protein Removal (Foam Fractionation)

Sub-micron particulate matter, fish mucus, surface-active proteins, and organic colour molecules cannot be intercepted by mechanical screens. High-efficiency Venturi-driven protein skimmers generate millions of microscopic bubbles. Surface-active compounds adhere to the rising bubble interfaces, forming a thick, dark biological foam concentrate that discharges out the top waste riser.

4. Degassing & Carbon Dioxide Stripping

As fish respire, dissolved carbon dioxide (CO₂) accumulates in the culture water. When dissolved CO₂ exceeds 15–20 mg/L, it induces hypercapnia, acidifies the blood, and impedes oxygen uptake. Counter-current packed-column degassing towers with high-volume low-pressure blowers efficiently strip dissolved CO₂ into the exhaust air before water re-enters the culture tanks.

5. Pure Oxygen Dissolution (Pressurized Oxygen Cones)

Atmospheric aeration cannot sustain super-intensive fish biomass. Deep Blue Aqua integrates high-pressure oxygen dissolution cones capable of achieving over 95% gas absorption efficiency. Pure industrial or PSA-generated oxygen gas is dissolved under pressure, delivering return water supersaturated at 120% to 180% DO, ensuring culture tanks never drop below 80% saturation (6.5 to 8.5 mg/L) even during peak post-feeding oxygen consumption surges.

6. Pathogen Biosecurity & Sterilization (Ozone & UV)

Closed-loop systems are vulnerable to pathogen proliferation if microbial populations are unmanaged. High-output germicidal ultraviolet (UV-C) reactors operating at 254 nm wavelength deliver minimum doses of 30 to 45 mJ/cm², effectively disrupting the DNA of waterborne bacteria, viruses, and parasites. In marine and shellfish facilities, low-dose micro-ozonation further clarifies water, eliminates lingering organic colour, and destroys free-swimming ciliates without toxic residuals.

Key Commercial Advantages of Closed RAS Technology

Why are progressive commercial growers and investors throughout South Africa and internationally choosing RAS over conventional earthen ponds and open flow-through waterways?

  • Unmatched Water Conservation: Water usage is reduced by up to 99%, allowing multi-ton production facilities to operate sustainably on low-yielding agricultural boreholes.
  • Guaranteed Biosecurity: Fully isolated from coastal dinoflagellate blooms (red tides), river agricultural pesticide runoff, and wild parasites.
  • Year-Round Optimal Growth: Complete water temperature control (using commercial heat pumps) eliminates seasonal growth plateaus, slashing grow-out cycles and optimizing Feed Conversion Ratios (FCR).
  • Geographic Independence: Facilities can be built directly adjacent to major urban markets, international airports, and logistics hubs, slashing live fish freight costs and eliminating cold-chain transport stress.

Deep Blue Aqua Turnkey Engineering & Commissioning

Building a successful commercial RAS requires seamless integration of biology and hydraulics. Deep Blue Aqua provides end-to-end design, AutoCAD fabrication, electrical telemetry manufacturing, on-site mechanical installation, and biological start-up seeding. From Franschhoek salmonid hatcheries to commercial marine holding on the Atlantic coast, our systems are built to withstand the toughest African industrial operating conditions while delivering unmatched biological safety.
